text:
Transmission Lines | Technical Procedure
Introduction
The
 purpose of this procedure is to provide detailed safe method for transmission
 lines maintenance staff to minimize the possibility of error causing personal
 injury or damage to equipment to measure the Earthing resistance using Megger.
EEA
 TL engineers in head office and zones using their background field experience
 and EEA documentation to create this procedure.
Safety Precautions
A
 work permit must be issued.
Inspect
 the used cables before use.
Wear
 safety shoes and rubber gloves.
Dont
 touch any bare conductor during measuring operation.
Tools and Equipment
Megger
 Earth tester (crank type).
Two
 probes.
Work to be Carried Out
Note: 
 In case of angle tower put the propes in the line that bisects the out side
 angle.
If it is not possible we can put them on the line that bisect the inside
 angle.
Put
 a jumper between the earth lead and the tower leg then separate the earth
 lead from the tower leg .
Release
 the jumper from the tower.
Connect
 the system as in figure no. (1) by putting the two probes and the earth at a
 straight line per 
 pendicular to the direction of the line to prevent any
 error due to induction
Adjust
 the pointer of the megger to the zero point
Running
 fastely the megger crank by hand.
Read
 and record the value of the resistance from the scale.
Repeat
 the measuring two times to ensure correct measuring.
Connect
 a jumper a cross the tower leg and earth lead then connect the earth lead to
 the
tower then disconnect the jumper from the two sides.
N.B The tower 
Earthing resistance must be less than or equal to 0.5 
ohm.
